n: Everyone should respect governing authorities, Paul says, because ultimately all authority exists under God. Christians in Rome lived under Nero’s early, relatively stable years. The JST applies these opening verses to authority in the Church.

f.w: be subject unto the higher powers

n: So whoever rebels against rightful authority resists what God has established and brings judgment on themselves.
Rulers aren’t a threat to people who do good, but to wrongdoers. Want to live without fear of the authorities? Do good, and you will earn their approval.

f.w: rulers are not a terror to good works

n: A ruler is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid — the authorities don’t carry the sword for nothing; they punish evildoers on God’s behalf.

f.w: beareth not the sword in vain
f.g: The sword symbolized a government’s power to punish.

n: So obey, not only to avoid punishment but because your conscience tells you it’s right.
That’s also why you pay taxes — officials are God’s servants who devote themselves to governing.

f.g: Taxes paid to a ruling power.

n: Give everyone what you owe them: taxes, revenue, respect, and honor. Jesus taught, “Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar’s.”

f.w: Render therefore to all their dues

n: Leave no debt unpaid except the ongoing debt to love one another — a debt we can never fully pay off. Love fulfills the law.

f.w: he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law

n: The commandments against adultery, murder, theft, false witness, and coveting are all summed up in one: love your neighbor as yourself.

f.w: Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill
Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself

n: Love never harms a neighbor. That’s why love fulfills the whole law.

f.w: love is the fulfilling of the law

n: Understand the times: it’s time to wake up from sleep! Our final salvation is closer now than when we first believed.

f.w: high time to awake out of sleep

n: The night is nearly over; the day is almost here. So throw off the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Live decently, as people do in daylight — not in wild partying and drunkenness, sexual immorality and indecency, or quarreling and jealousy.
Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and don’t plan ways to gratify your fleshly desires. Augustine famously turned to Christ after reading this verse.

f.w: put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ
make not provision for the flesh
f.g: Don’t make plans or room for indulging sinful desires.
